substantive_reconstruction.infinite_counterexample: Let K=C(t), G=K^times and V=K over C. Multiplication by g preserves C-linear combinations, is inverted by multiplication by g^-1, and respects the group law. G is abelian. A finite relation among1,t,t²,... would be a zero polynomial in an indeterminate, so their C-linear independence proves infinite dimension. If invariant W contains w!=0, then every nonzero v equals(v/w)w for v/w in G; hence W=V. This verifies irreducibility rather than inferring it from a large orbit name or using a reducible trivial action. Multiplication by t has no complex eigenvalue: t-lambda is invertible in K for every lambda.
substantive_reconstruction.finite_positive_proof: For fixed h, abelianness gives rho(h)rho(g)=rho(g)rho(h). Positive finite dimension makes the characteristic polynomial of the LINEAR rho(h) nonconstant; algebraic closure gives a root lambda and a nonzero kernel for rho(h)-lambda I. Commutation makes that kernel invariant, so irreducibility makes it all of V. Every rho(h) is scalar. For any nonzero v, Cv is invariant under every group element and therefore equals V. This proves dimension1 without simultaneous diagonalization, group averaging, finiteness of G, unitarity or division by its order.
substantive_reconstruction.character_and_field: On nonzero V each scalar is unique and nonzero because rho(h) is invertible. Representation identities applied to v give lambda_gh=lambda_g lambda_h and lambda_e=1; the inverse scalar follows too. Conversely a homomorphism G->C^times acts irreducibly on C because a line has no proper nonzero linear subspace. The same argument works over ANY algebraically closed field, including positive characteristic: no trace or characteristic-zero operation occurs. Eigenvalues for every particular action operator would also suffice; closure is a uniform sufficient field condition, not necessary for every individual representation.
substantive_reconstruction.real_and_zero_witnesses: The C4 generator J=[[0,-1],[1,0]] satisfies J4=I and acts orthogonally on R². If a proper nonzero invariant real line had generator v, then Jv=a v for real a, giving -v=a²v, impossible. Thus it is a genuine irreducible two-dimensional real action, unlike identity or half-turn rotations. Over C its eigenlines remove this counterexample. If the invariant-subspace predicate permits V0, it is vacuously irreducible but dimension0; the positive theorem explicitly excludes it and does not invent an eigenvector. No topology or bounded/Hilbert-space realization is claimed for C(t), so continuous/unitary Schur variants are not contradicted.
